figures.finding: A Chilean resident pays the annual Global Complementary Tax, progressive in annual tax units (UTA): nothing to 13.5 UTA, then 4%, 8%, 13.5%, 23%, 30.4%, 35%, and 40% above 310 UTA; there is no local income tax.
figures.applies: 2026. The same bands monthly in UTM give the employment tax (Impuesto Único de Segunda Categoría); PwC's table at 35.5% top is dated 2017 and not used.

sources.said: Noviembre 72.440 869.280
There are no local income taxes to be paid in Chile, only central government taxes.

figures.finding: The employer withholds the monthly employment tax by the SII table; for November 2026 nothing is due on monthly taxable pay up to CLP 977,940 (13.5 UTM), then 4% up to 40% above CLP 22,456,400. A freelancer's fee invoice (boleta de honorarios) bears 15.25% withholding in 2026 (16% in 2027, 17% from 2028).
figures.applies: Monthly table changes with the UTM each month.

La ley 21.133 establece que a partir del 1 de enero de 2026 el porcentaje de retención pasa de 14,5% a 15,25% llegando a 17% en 2028.

figures.finding: An employee pays about 20% of salary (pension, health and related) on pay up to UF 75.7 a month, and 0.6% unemployment insurance (employer 2.4%) up to UF 113.5; the employer also pays a 0.93% accident premium plus a risk surcharge.
figures.applies: Foreigners covered by a home scheme may be exempt. The fee-earner's 15.25% retention funds the self-employed's compulsory contributions under Ley 21.133.

sources.said: salaries are subject to Chilean social security contribution of 20%, computed on the monthly salary capped at 75.7 unidades de fomento
of 3% in connection with unemployment insurance (0.6% contributed by the employee and 2.4% contributed by the employer) with a cap of UF 113.5
a monthly 0.93% premium on remuneration

figures.finding: A non-resident performer, writer or director paid for cultural work done in Chile bears a 20% additional tax on the whole fee with no deduction, withheld by whoever hired them before they leave; it is a single, final tax replacing the second-category tax. Other non-resident income bears 35% (15% for technical or professional services per PwC).
figures.applies: Non-resident individuals with cultural, scientific or sporting activities in Chile (Ley sobre Impuesto a la Renta art. 60, inciso 2). The SII's copy of the law is updated to Ley 21.047 (2017); later amendments to art. 60 are not shown in it.

sources.said: pagarán respecto de ellas un impuesto adicional de 35%. … No obstante, la citada tasa será de 20% cuando se trate de remuneraciones provenientes exclusivamente del trabajo o habilidad de personas, percibidas por las personas naturales a que se refiere el inciso anterior, sólo cuando éstas hubieren desarrollado en Chile actividades científicas, culturales o deportivas. Este impuesto deberá ser retenido y pagado antes de que dichas personas se ausenten del país, por quien o quienes contrataron sus servicios, de acuerdo con las normas de los artículos 74 y 79. … El impuesto establecido en este artículo tendrá el carácter de impuesto único a la renta respecto de las rentas referidas en el inciso segundo, en reemplazo del impuesto de la Segunda Categoría, y se aplicará sobre las cantidades que se paguen, se abonen en cuenta o se pongan a disposición de las personas mencionadas en dicho inciso, sin deducción alguna.

Before residence is acquired, a flat 15% tax generally is levied if the activities can be qualified as technical or engineering work or professional services that an individual renders through a report, advice, or plan development. In the case of other activities, or where the paying company is located in a tax haven, other rates would apply.
nonresident individuals are taxed only on their Chilean- source income.

figures.finding: VAT is 19% on transfers and services.
figures.applies: In the SII's 2017 text a 'service' for VAT is one from the activities of LIR art. 20 Nos. 3 and 4 (commerce, industry and the like), which leaves an individual's honorarios (second-category income, LIR art. 42 No. 2) outside VAT; the 2022 reform widening VAT to services (Ley 21.420) is not in that copy, so the current treatment is still open (see blocker).

sources.said: Por “servicio”, la acción o prestación que una persona realiza para otra y por la cual percibe un interés, prima, comisión o cualquiera otra forma de remuneración, siempre que provenga del ejercicio de las actividades comprendidas en los Nºs. 3 y 4, del artículo 20, de la Ley sobre Impuesto a la Renta.
VAT is payable on transfers and services at a rate of 19%.
The standard VAT rate is 19%.

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year; the annual return is filed, and any tax paid, in April of the following year.
figures.applies: Due date read as the end of April.

sources.said: Tax year: The tax year is a calendar year. Filing status:
An annual income tax return must be filed in April of the year following the end of the tax year, and any tax due must be paid at that time.
